text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. Developers refactor code to make it cleaner and easier to understand. This improves readability, so other programmers can work with it more easily. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly and becomes messy over time. For example, you might rename variables, split long functions into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. The key rule is that the program's behavior must stay the same. Refactoring is like cleaning a room: everything still works, but it is much nicer to use.
